_comment: PRD §10 'Upgrades'. The five entries the §10 example table prices explicitly (Serving Tray I/II, Faster Grill I, Better Seating, Pantry Shelves) carry those costs and effects verbatim; the rest fill out the §10 category table. `serving_tray_1` and `faster_grill_1` are the ids the §12 `setup_submit` and `purchase_upgrade` examples reference, so they are not renameable. §10 caps MVP at three tiers per category and forbids exponential chains — `tier` is 1 unless the upgrade supersedes a cheaper one, in which case `requires` names it. `effects` is machine-readable: every key is a value a system reads, never prose. Multipliers are 1.0-relative, so a duration multiplier BELOW 1 is faster. Upgrades are purchased in-world at `upgrade_terminal` in the §14 layout, which is what makes spending cash cost time.

upgrades.name: Serving Tray I
upgrades.description: The owner carries two plates per run instead of one.

upgrades.name: Serving Tray II
upgrades.description: The owner carries three plates per run. Strong during group-rush events.

upgrades.name: Better Seating
upgrades.description: Seated patience +15%. Gives the server room to recover.

upgrades.name: Prep Counter
upgrades.description: A second prep slot, so prep stops being the single-file bottleneck.

upgrades.name: Server Radio
upgrades.description: The server picks better targets and wastes fewer trips.

upgrades.name: Additional Table
upgrades.description: One more two-top. More seats, but also more for one server to cover.

upgrades.name: Street Signage
upgrades.description: Improves consideration among undecided customers in the district.

upgrades.name: Maintenance Plan
upgrades.description: Halves the chance a station fails mid-service.

upgrades.name: Complimentary Snacks
upgrades.description: A comp recovers more satisfaction and can be offered more often.
